inputs.original_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement is another warning that students and families are being made to bear the cost of a dispute between government and union leaders. The government should meet its obligations, but it must also uphold order and insist that education is not held hostage by threats of an indefinite nationwide strike. A responsible settlement matters; so does putting students’ future ahead of political pressure.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement shows how students and families are too often caught in the crossfire when unions and government fail to resolve their disputes. The government should honor its obligations, but it must also protect the authority of schools and refuse to let threats of an indefinite nationwide strike dictate terms. Education is a public trust, not a bargaining chip; union leaders and officials alike should put students’ futures and the stability families depend on ahead of political pressure.
